items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: asked Carmen Masfrjen and myself, the guitar player, Carmen Masfrjen, if we'd see if Tommy would play this demo.

ctx.x: It took us about two and a half to three hours to fly to Toronto from Newark, which is usually about a 40 minute trip today. And going over the mountains, they flew at pretty low altitudes then, into Buffalo and into Toronto, the air currents are pretty bad. However, it was quite an experience, and I remember at the Exposition, we played in a tent then, and I believe that they built

buildings now where it's a yearly annual thing. And we played in a huge tent, and it was a young crippled lady in a wheelchair that came back and asked us if we would play a demo, asked Carmen Masfrjen and myself, the guitar player, Carmen Masfrjen, if we'd see if Tommy would play this demo.

Well, when we returned to New York, we tried for about a week or two to get Tom, between sets, to go into a back room that we had up at the Pennsylvania Roof and listen to this record. And we couldn't get him to do it, but eventually he came in and listened to it, and that song turned out to be 'I'll Never Smile Again,' which after I left in a few months, Frank recorded, and I guess that's the story of that.
